title: The Distributive Property: Multiplying Across Parentheses
subject: Mathematics
text: The Distributive Property states that multiplying a factor across a sum or difference requires applying the multiplier to every term inside the parentheses: a(b + c) = ab + ac. When the multiplier is a negative quantity, each term inside the parentheses must be multiplied by that negative number, reversing the signs: -a(b + c) = -ab - ac, and -a(b - c) = -ab + ac. A frequent misconception is multiplying only the first term and leaving subsequent terms unchanged, such as writing -2(x + 3) = -2x + 3 instead of distributing the -2 to both x and +3 to obtain -2x - 6. Always multiply the outer factor by each internal term individually before simplifying.
